title: Latency outlier heatmap, rapid RCA and staged mitigation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Several customers across Hosted, Dedicated and Private reported intermittent first-token latency regressions and drops in tokens/sec over the last 36 hours. This ticket drives a fast RCA derived from a latency heatmap, implements short-term mitigations that are safe to roll out rapidly, and tracks follow-up permanent fixes. Goal: restore p50/p95 TTFT and tokens/sec to baseline within the outage window and avoid cascading customer impact.
investigation_summary: What we observed: a concentrated set of latency outliers between 01:30-03:00 UTC and again at 11:00-12:00 UTC correlated with tenant fanout spikes and model variant probe activity. Heatmap analysis (1-minute bins, 12-hour window) shows sharp vertical bands affecting a subset of tenants in Dedicated and Private clusters; Hosted shows wider, lower-amplitude tail spikes. Metrics correlated: TTFT p99 up from 220ms->1.6s; tokens/sec median drop ~35% during peaks; kernel switch counts spiked and NVCache evictions increased by 4x. Key hypothesis: asynchronous weight/variant re-probing combined with kernel-selector misallocation caused temporary kernel preemption and KV cache thrash on specific GPU types (A100nv vs A10G), amplifying warmstart latency. This was exacerbated in Private because a recent rebalancer job (rb-2026-03-09) initiated cross-shard weight swaps at 01:15 UTC causing concurrent warmstart churn.
repro_steps: Replay load on staging with tenant fanning pattern (multiply tenant X traffic by 8) for 15 minutes using the 'fanout-heavy' replay script: scripts/replay/fanout-heavy.sh
Enable variant probing in staging (env VARIANT_PROBE=1) and set kernel selector to heuristic mode (KERNEL_SELECTOR=heuristic) to reproduce the kernel-switch churn
Observe TTFT and tokens/sec via dashboard: /dashboards/latency/heatmap?env=staging&window=1h
Run synthetic multi-model fanout test against a Dedicated-style topology (2 models, 4 replicas each) with randomized weight swaps at 1-min intervals to provoke NVCache eviction behavior
mitigation_plan: Immediate (10-30m): Deploy a configuration patch that caps per-tenant fanout to 4 for affected clusters; this is a config-only change and reversible. (PR: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4389)

Short term (1-3h): Roll back kernel-selector to v2.11 heuristic on Dedicated/private clusters (rollback flag kernel.selector=v2.11) to avoid aggressive kernel preemption while we validate new selector heuristics
Short term (1-6h): Gate asynchronous re-probing job 'rb-2026-03-09' and schedule weight swaps during low-traffic windows; coordinate with infra release manager
Monitoring: Add temporary alert: p99 TTFT > 900ms for >5m trigger and tokens/sec drop >20% across >3 hosts. Add a heatmap tile in Console runbook for quick triage
Customer comms: Notify impacted customers via bridge and follow up with a remediation timeline and mitigations applied
rollout_plan: Canary 1 (Hoster-managed clusters): 1% traffic, 30m observation window, monitor p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec
Canary 2 (Dedicated): 5% traffic, 30m observation window, expand if stable
Full rollout: 100% on Dedicated/Private within 3 hours if no regressions; Hosted targeted separately after Dedicated stability confirmed
Rollback criterion: any canary shows p99 increase >200ms vs baseline or tokens/sec drop >15% sustained for 10m
